songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Fiery Golden Road → New Potato flow, tight early jams
ai_show_review.blurb: A short, high‑energy four‑song set that rolls from The Golden Road into New Potato Caboose and Alligator before a heartfelt He Was A Friend Of Mine. Jerry’s guitar is on fire, Phil’s bass drives the grooves, and Pigpen adds warm organ texture. The best‑sounding board capture highlights the band’s loose, early‑1967 vibe.
ai_show_review.review: On May 5, 1967 at the Fillmore Auditorium the Dead delivered a blistering four‑song set that captures the band in a transitional, electrified phase. Opening with “The Golden Road [To Unlimited Devotion]”, Jerry Garcia’s Gibson tones blaze through soaring solos while Phil Lesh’s bass is described as hot and on fire, laying down a propulsive foundation. The segue into “New Potato Caboose” feels seamless, and the band rides that momentum straight into a muscular “Alligator”. Pigpen’s organ work adds an amazing B‑3‑like whizz that warms the mix, even though the early board source shows some bass saturation and occasional muddiness. The set closes with a heartfelt rendition of “He Was A Friend Of Mine”, showcasing the three‑part vocal harmonies of Jerry, Bob Weir, and Phil. Among the three available recordings, the “gd67-05-05.sbs.yerys.1595.sbeok.shnf” capture stands out as the most complete and historically representative version, delivering clear enough sound to hear each instrument while preserving the raw excitement of that night.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality early board/audience capture that includes the full four‑song set with clear instrument separation despite minor bass saturation; regarded as one of the better recordings from this transitional period.

key_highlights: Fiery guitar work and soaring solos on The Golden Road
Tight, seamless flow into New Potato Caboose and Alligator
Warm, whizzing Pigpen organ that adds depth to the set
Strong vocal harmonies on He Was A Friend Of Mine
song_highlights: He Was A Friend Of Mine

band_performance.Jerry: Fiery Gibson tone, soaring solos and overall fire; early free‑loose playing shines throughout the set.
band_performance.Phil: Hot, driving bass that underpins the jams and adds a blazing low end.
band_performance.Bob: Contributes solid rhythm guitar and blends in three‑part vocal harmonies with Jerry and Phil.
band_performance.Billy: Artistic drumming that anchors the band; solid despite occasional mix mud from the two‑drummer setup.

must_listen_sequences: He Was A Friend Of Mine
